channel.title: Bloomberg — Reuters/Bloomberg pool
channel.description: Provenance-aware feed; classification fields distinguish exact wire copies from citations.

item.title: JBS Seeks Rest of Pilgrim’s Pride Stake in $1.2 Billion Deal
item.description: Pilgrim’s Pride Corp. shares jumped after meatpacking giant JBS NV offered to acquire the shares of the chicken producer it doesn’t already own in a stock deal valued at about $1.2 billion.
item.dc:creator: Dayanne Sousa

item.title: China Bonds Buck Global Selloff on Policy Divide With Peers
item.description: A relentless drop in China’s long-end yields is driving an aggressive curve flattening, laying bare a stark macro rift with global markets where long-dated rates have hit multi-year peaks.
item.dc:creator: Julia Zhong and Shulun Huang

item.title: Hong Kong Exchanges’ Non-Equity Push Seen as Key for Stock Boost
item.description: With record trading volumes and new listings providing little boost for shares of Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing Ltd., analysts are increasingly looking for a jolt from the company’s expansion of non-equity business.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu and Iris Ouyang

item.title: Japan’s Earnings Surprise Analysts to Fuel Bets for Broad Rally
item.description: Japanese companies posted their largest earnings beat in five years despite soaring oil costs, fueling hopes that strong profit growth across sectors can broaden the market rally beyond AI-related trades.
item.dc:creator: Hideyuki Sano

item.title: Roz Brewer Talks College Aid, Walgreens During Covid and Retail
item.description: Spelman College Chair Emerita Rosalind "Roz" Brewer, former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance, says that she "never looked back to the lab" after moving from working as an organic chemist at Kimberly-Clarke to moving to the corporate side of the business. Speaking to Romaine Bostick at Bloomberg New Voices in Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts, Brewer says that the timing of her joining Walgreens during the Covid-19 pandemic gave her the best chance to make changes, as times of crisis often provide the best opportunities to do so. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chip Selloff Clouds Asia Open, Bond Jitters Linger: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to fall as a selloff in US technology shares, elevated bond yields and rising oil prices weighed on sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Gluten-Free Brand Breaks Out in Saturated Market
item.description: Feel Good Foods has been selling gluten-free frozen foods since 2012, eventually starting to outsell legacy frozen food brands like PF Chang's and TGI Fridays. CEO Vanessa Phillips founded the brand after being diagnosed with celiac disease and college, and refusing to give up her favorite foods. She says the brand doesn't just serve gluten-free consumers, saying most customers buy the product because it "works for them and their lifestyle." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
item.description: Oil rose for a fourth day, with no sign of progress toward a resolution of the US-Iran war after almost six months of conflict.
item.dc:creator: Rong Wei Neo

item.title: Roz Brewer Says US Retail Needs Global Partners
item.description: Spelman College Chair Emerita Rosalind "Roz" Brewer, former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance, discusses the state of the US consumer in the current economy with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg New Voices event in Martha’s Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Revolution's Hall On Investing in the Defense Sector
item.description: David Hall, managing partner at Revolution, talks about investing in the defense sector and backing Hermeus, a company looking to build a hyper-sonic military jet. He speaks with Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg New Voices event in Martha's Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Falls as Traders Weigh US Inflation
item.description: Gold valuation platform Unvault estimates that American households are sitting on $750 Billion worth of gold, largely in the form of unworn jewelry. The company says consumers consistently underestimate their jewelry's spot value by 3x or more because pieces purchased prior to 2010 have more than tripled in value. CEO Nidhi Singhvi joins Businessweek Daily to discuss how her business is being boosting by higher gold prices in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fletcher Building Waits on Meaningful Recovery in NZ Demand
item.description: New Zealand’s largest construction materials company Fletcher Building Ltd. doesn’t expect a meaningful recovery in its markets until 2027, adding to signs of muted economic growth over the second half of this year.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: Uruguay Holds Interest Rates Steady With Inflation Below Target
item.description: Uruguay’s central bank held interest rates steady for a fourth consecutive policy meeting with inflation below its target.
item.dc:creator: Ken Parks

item.title: Power Broker Frances Katzen on Pending Home Sales Slide
item.description: Frances Katzen, founder of The Katzen Team and a top broker at Douglas Elliman in New York City, discussed the current dynamics of the housing market, highlighting a pronounced K-shaped trend. While overall housing activity has slowed, the high-end segment in Manhattan is experiencing significant growth, with contract signings up 39% year-over-year in October and properties priced between $3 million and $5 million up 27%. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: KKR Real Estate Lender’s Woes Attract Investment Firm Mavik
item.description: An investment firm that specializes in commercial real estate distress is betting that a lender managed by KKR & Co. is likely to sell its loan portfolio at or around book value.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Clark

item.title: Ex-Tricolor Executives Face SEC Lawsuit After Firm Collapse
item.description: Tricolor Holdings founder Daniel Chu, who already faces federal criminal charges, and two other former executives were sued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission for allegedly defrauding investors before the used car seller and subprime lender imploded.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Walter Probe Weighs on Carvana as Traders Suspect Share Sale
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. dropped Tuesday, hurt by concerns that one of the company’s largest investors — billionaire Mark Walter — may sell down his stake as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.
item.dc:creator: Georgie McKay

item.title: Bond Traders Bite at Microsoft-Tied Data Center Junk-Like Yields
item.description: Blackstone Inc.-backed QTS Realty Trust Inc. offered junk-like yields on a $3.9 billion high-grade bond to fund the construction of a Microsoft Corp.-linked data center in Georgia. It looks to have worked as the deal racked up demand of about six times that amount.
item.dc:creator: Brian Smith and Davide Barbuscia

item.title: Energy Stocks Hit Record as Oil Rises on Fading Deal Hopes
item.description: Energy stocks closed at the first record since March as investors see diminishing prospects for a near-term ceasefire in the Iran war that could ease the standoff in the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Monique Mulima

item.title: EM Rally Stalls Amid Surge in Treasury Yields, Mideast Tensions
item.description: The recent rally in emerging-market assets stalled on Tuesday as a surge in long-term US Treasury yields and renewed tensions in the Middle East drained demand for risk, snapping a four-day winning streak in stocks and pushing borrowing costs higher.
item.dc:creator: David Feliba and Peter Laca
